pr.title: Only update `Eq` operands in GVN if it can update both sides
pr.description:
Otherwise the types might not match

Fixes #127089

r? mir-opt

issues.title: ICE: Cannot Eq compare incompatible types *mut T/#0 and *const T/#0
issues.body:
Compiling the following code with `rustc -C opt-level=3 -o main main.rs` results in ICE. Strangely, this code compiles fine **without** `-C opt-level=3`. Replace `std::ptr::eq` with plain `==` comparison also works. ### Code `main.rs`: ```Rust #![feature(strict_provenance)] struct Foo(std::marker::PhantomData); impl Foo { const SENTINEL: *mut T = std::ptr::dangling_mut(); fn cmp_ptr(a: *mut T) -> bool { std::ptr::eq(a, Self::SENTINEL) } } pub fn main() { Foo::::cmp_ptr(std::ptr::dangling_mut()); } ``` ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.81.0-nightly (9c3bc805d 2024-06-27) binary: rustc commit-hash: 9c3bc805dd9cb84019c124b9a50fdff1e62a7ec9 commit-date: 2024-06-27 host: aarch64-apple-darwin release: 1.81.0-nightly LLVM version: 18.1.7 ``` ### Error output ``` thread 'rustc' panicked at compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/validate.rs:94:25: broken MIR in Item(DefId(0:10 ~ main[a0a6]::{impl#0}::cmp_ptr)) (after phase change to runtime-optimized) at bb0[2]: Cannot Eq compare incompatible types *mut T/#0 and *const T/#0 ```

processing.reason: The historical GVN bug is a type-consistency failure, not a value-changing miscompilation. In the regression shape `_3 = (*_1) as *const u8; _4 = _2 as *const u8; _0 = Eq(_3, _4)`, the old per-side `try_as_operand` rewrite can replace only `_4` with `_2` (type `*mut u8`) while leaving `_3` as `*const u8`, producing the ill-typed comparison `Eq(*mut u8, *const u8)` and the reported validation ICE. The corrected code either rewrites both operands or neither. `try_as_operand` is value-preserving: the replaced operand denotes the same pointer address, and `PtrToPtr` casts preserve the address (and metadata). Therefore any source-level simulation that still type-checks compares the same addresses and returns the same bool for every defined input. The only faithful encoding of the wrong transformation is an ill-typed MIR comparison (or a forced transmute of identical pointer bits), which cannot produce a Miri-passing pair with a genuinely different original/transformed runtime value. Manufacturing a bool difference would require adding unrelated semantics not justified by PR #127105.

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's simplify_binary, when both operands of an `Eq` are resolvable to values, independently attempted to materialize each side as an operand: `if let Some(op) = self.try_as_operand(lhs, location) { *lhs_operand = op; } if let Some(op) = self.try_as_operand(rhs, location) { *rhs_operand = op; }`. Each side could therefore be constant-folded or rewritten on its own.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: GVN rewrote only one side of an `Eq` (`_1 = Eq(_4, _6)`) into a constant operand while leaving the other side as a pointer/cast operand, producing an ill-typed comparison. The historical wrong rewrite arose exactly when `try_as_operand` succeeded for one side and failed for the other: the surviving operand kept type `*mut T` while the rewritten side became `*const T`, yielding `Cannot Eq compare incompatible types *mut T/#0 and *const T/#0`. The corrected transformation only updates both operands when both `try_as_operand` calls succeed: `if let Some(lhs_op) = self.try_as_operand(lhs, location) && let Some(rhs_op) = self.try_as_operand(rhs, location) { *lhs_operand = lhs_op; *rhs_operand = rhs_op; }`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR binary `Eq`/comparison terms where both operands are values (locals/constants) but their types differ, notably raw-pointer comparisons involving `*mut T` vs `*const T` and casts (`PtrToPtr`, `Transmute`). In the reported case, `std::ptr::eq(a, Self::SENTINEL)` after inlining `cmp_ptr` and `dangling_mut` exposes a `*const u8` cast result compared against a constant pointee, with the other side still a `*mut u8`-derived value.
analysis.summary: Historical bug fix in GVN: trying to replace operands of an `Eq` binary op independently could rewrite one side and leave the other unchanged, violating Eq's same-type requirement and causing an ICE ("Cannot Eq compare incompatible types"). The fix makes both operand updates conditional on both `try_as_operand` conversions succeeding.
analysis.trigger: In GVN's binary simplification, both operands are values and at least one can be converted by `try_as_operand` while the other cannot; the per-side rewrite then changes the types asymmetrically. Triggered by code like `std::ptr::eq(a, Self::SENTINEL)` with `SENTINEL: *mut T = std::ptr::dangling_mut()` after inlining `cmp_ptr` and `dangling_mut`.
preconditions: GVN simplification reaches simplify_binary for an Eq/comparison term whose operands are both values
One operand can be materialized as an operand via try_as_operand and the other cannot (or the two sides have different pointer types)
Inlining (e.g. cmp_ptr, dangling_mut) has exposed casts such as `(*_1) as *const u8 (PtrToPtr)` and `_2 as *const u8 (PtrToPtr)` alongside constant sentinels
strict_provenance / raw pointer equality code path, as in the issue's std::ptr::eq example
pitfalls: Updating each operand independently is unsound when the transformation is type-sensitive: an Eq term requires both operands to have the same type
A test that simply checks both casts remain is not enough: the key invariant is all-or-nothing rewriting of the two Eq operands, not merely preserving one cast
The MIR diff for remove_casts_must_change_both_sides is identical before and after GVN; that shows no rewrite occurred, not that the pass executed a different valid rewrite
Do not conflate the pointer-cast borrowing/overwrite concerns with the actual type-consistency bug; the fix is about joint operand update
The regression relies on Inline (`-Z mir-enable-passes=+Inline`) plus GVN to expose the problematic comparison; testing only one pass may miss the condition
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR-opt regression with `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` (and, for the reported ICE, `-Z mir-enable-passes=+Inline`). Construct two related cases: (1) a `#[custom_mir(dialect = "analysis")]` function where two `PtrToPtr` casts feed `Eq`, checking that GVN leaves both casts intact (`[[A]] = (*_1) as *const u8`, `[[B]] = _2 as *const u8`, `_0 = Eq([[A]], [[B]])`) because neither side can be replaced; and (2) the strict-provenance `Foo::<T>::cmp_ptr`/`dangling_mut` case checking that after inlining+GVN the comparison folds consistently to a constant (`_6 = const {0x1 as *const u8}; _1 = const true`). The differentiating transformation for a separate agent is: independently rewriting whichever Eq side `try_as_operand` succeeds on, versus requiring both sides to rewrite together. A negative test should detect mismatched operand types / validation failure rather than assume a specific extra rewrite.
evidence: Only update `Eq` operands in GVN if it can update both sides
Otherwise the types might not match
// We'd like to remove these casts, but we can't change *both* of them
// to be locals, so make sure we don't change one without the other, as
// that would be a type error.
Cannot Eq compare incompatible types *mut T/#0 and *const T/#0
Replace `std::ptr::eq` with plain `==` comparison also works.
